transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, what brings me in is that I've just gotten... really slowed down lately. I'm an auditor, and it's gotten to the point where I can sit staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's like I just can't get going. And, well, people at work have started noticing that I'm not keeping up with my usual pace.
Beyond just feeling slowed down at work, how has your mood been lately? Would you say you've been feeling sad, empty, or down?

Yeah, I have been. Empty is probably a good word for it. Most days, um, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It just feels like... well, like the day is already lost before I've even managed to get out of bed.
How long have you been feeling this way — this emptiness and slowness? Has it been going on for a few weeks now, or longer?

It's been longer than a few weeks. Um, this has been going on for about seven months now. It started around the time my husband stopped working... he lost his job during a downsizing at his company, and things just haven't been the same since then.

Besides the slowness and emptiness you've described, have you noticed that things you normally enjoy — hobbies, time with friends, activities you used to look forward to — just don't interest you anymore?

Yeah, I have. Um, I used to do a lot of different things. I would plan hikes, take photos, cook on Sundays, and I even volunteered at the library. But now... I don't know, none of it really appeals to me. All of those things just feel like items on a checklist that I don't care enough to even start.
How has your sleep been during these past seven months? Are you sleeping more, less, or about the same as you normally would?
Um, I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't really noticed a big change either way. I guess I'm sleeping about the same as I always have.
Have you been blaming yourself or feeling guilty about your husband losing his job, or feeling like you're a burden to him?

No, I don't think so. I mean, the downsizing was just something that happened at his company, so I know that wasn't my fault. And... no, I haven't really felt like a burden to him, either. I don't really have those kinds of thoughts, it's just that everything feels so empty right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over these past seven months?

Yeah, I have. Um, food has mostly just become something I force down, really. Only because I know I should eat. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, but my work skirts have definitely gotten loose on me lately.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you were dead?
No, I haven't. I mean, things feel really empty, like I said, but I don't want to die. I haven't had any thoughts about hurting myself.

You mentioned sitting and staring at your workpapers for long periods — beyond just the slowness, have you noticed it's harder to concentrate or focus your thoughts, or do you find yourself more forgetful than usual?

No, not really. I mean, my memory seems fine, I haven't been forgetting things. And I don't think it's that I can't focus... it's more just that I sit there and stare. I know exactly what I need to do with the spreadsheets, I just... don't do it. So, no, my concentration itself seems okay, I think.

When you're sitting there staring at the workpaper, does your body itself feel heavy or sluggish — like your arms and legs are moving in slow motion — or is it more that you just don't feel motivated to start?

Um, no, my body doesn't feel heavy. It's not a physical thing where my arms or legs are moving in slow motion or anything like that. Physically, I feel fine. It's... yeah, it's definitely more that I just don't have the motivation to actually start doing it.
During these past seven months, have there been any stretches of time — maybe a few weeks or longer — where you felt noticeably better, where the emptiness lifted a bit or your mood improved?

No, not really. It's just been a steady... emptiness, I guess, for the whole seven months. I haven't really had any breaks where I felt better or where things lifted. It's just been the same every day.

Have there ever been periods in your life — even before these past seven months — when you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing or your mind was going faster than usual?

No, I've never had anything like that. I've always been pretty even-keeled, I guess. I've never had a time where I felt super energetic or didn't need to sleep. My mind doesn't really race... it's just, well, lately it's just been kind of blank. But no, never any periods of high energy like you're describing.
